items.followUp: List four functions of the liver and explain how it helps regulate blood glucose.

rubric.why: Bile production is a major liver function and aids fat digestion.
rubric.description: Produces bile, which helps in fat digestion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming bile production and its role in fat digestion.

rubric.why: The liver helps maintain blood glucose by storing glucose as glycogen and releasing it when needed.
rubric.description: Regulates blood glucose by converting glucose to glycogen and glycogen back to glucose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing this glucose–glycogen regulation.

rubric.why: The liver removes amino groups from excess amino acids and converts the resulting ammonia into urea.
rubric.description: Carries out deamination and forms urea.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking deamination of excess amino acids with urea formation.

rubric.why: Detoxification, storage of nutrients and breakdown of worn-out red blood cells are additional liver functions.
rubric.description: Performs other functions such as detoxification, nutrient storage and breakdown of worn-out red blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one of these additional functions.

modelAnswer: The liver produces bile, which helps in the digestion of fats.
It regulates blood glucose by converting glucose into glycogen for storage and glycogen back into glucose when needed.
It deaminates excess amino acids and forms urea from the nitrogenous waste.
It detoxifies harmful substances.
It stores vitamins and minerals, including iron.
It breaks down worn-out red blood cells.

items.followUp: Compare the structure and functions of the heart, arteries and veins.

rubric.why: Arteries have thicker, more elastic walls than veins; veins have thinner walls and a wider lumen.
rubric.description: Compares artery and vein walls or lumen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct structural comparison of arteries and veins.

rubric.why: Veins contain valves to prevent backflow; arteries generally do not.
rubric.description: Compares the presence of valves in arteries and veins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the valve difference.

rubric.why: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins return blood to it.
rubric.description: States the directions in which arteries and veins carry blood.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both directions correctly stated.

rubric.why: The very thin capillary wall permits exchange between blood and tissues.
rubric.description: Describes capillary walls as one cell thick.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the one-cell-thick wall.

rubric.why: Capillaries connect the arterial and venous sides and exchange materials with body cells.
rubric.description: Explains the exchange function of capillaries.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that capillaries exchange substances between blood and tissues.

modelAnswer: Arteries have thick, elastic walls and a relatively narrow lumen; veins have thinner walls and a wider lumen.
Veins have valves to prevent the backward flow of blood; arteries generally do not have valves.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins carry blood towards the heart.
Capillaries have extremely thin walls, only one cell thick, and connect small arteries with small veins.
Capillaries allow exchange of oxygen, nutrients and waste materials between blood and body tissues.

items.followUp: Name two major environmental or health challenges that biology helps us address.

rubric.why: Food supply and malnutrition are major biological challenges.
rubric.description: Identifies food shortage or malnutrition as a major issue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming food shortage, food insecurity or malnutrition.

rubric.why: Health, environmental and population challenges are among the major biological issues today.
rubric.description: Identifies another major biological issue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any other valid issue, such as disease, pollution, population growth or loss of biodiversity.

modelAnswer: Major biological issues today include food shortage and malnutrition.
Other important issues include diseases, environmental pollution, rapid population growth and loss of biodiversity.

items.followUp: Define agriculture and name two branches of it.

rubric.why: Horticulture concerns the cultivation of garden plants, including fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants.
rubric.description: Defines horticulture as the cultivation of garden plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining horticulture as the cultivation of garden plants or crops such as fruits, vegetables or ornamentals.

rubric.why: Horticulture is a branch of agriculture.
rubric.description: Explains horticulture's relationship to agriculture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that horticulture is a branch or specialized part of agriculture.

modelAnswer: Horticulture is the branch of biology and agriculture concerned with cultivating garden plants, such as fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants.
It is related to agriculture because it is a specialized branch of agriculture.

items.followUp: What are macromolecules? Give two examples found in living organisms.

rubric.why: Bioelements are the chemical elements that make up living organisms.
rubric.description: Defines bioelements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that bioelements are chemical elements present in or making up living organisms.

rubric.why: Carbon, oxygen, hydrogen, nitrogen, phosphorus and sulfur are examples of bioelements.
rubric.description: Gives two examples of bioelements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two valid examples.

modelAnswer: Bioelements are the chemical elements that make up living organisms.
Examples include carbon and oxygen.

items.followUp: In an experiment testing how light affects plant growth, identify the control and experimental groups.

rubric.why: The control group provides a baseline and is not exposed to the factor being tested.
rubric.description: Defines the control group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it does not receive the treatment or manipulated variable and serves as a comparison.

rubric.why: The experimental group receives the treatment or manipulated variable so its effect can be tested.
rubric.description: Defines the experimental group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it receives the treatment or manipulated variable.

modelAnswer: The control group is kept under normal conditions and does not receive the factor being tested; it provides a basis for comparison.
The experimental group receives the factor or treatment being tested.

items.followUp: State the mosquito hypothesis about malaria and give one observation that supported it.

rubric.why: A. F. A. King proposed that mosquitoes were involved in transmitting malaria.
rubric.description: States the main idea of King's hypothesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that mosquitoes transmit or spread malaria.

rubric.why: The question asks specifically for the hypothesis suggested by A. F. A. King.
rubric.description: Identifies the scientist associated with the hypothesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly attributing the hypothesis to A. F. A. King.

modelAnswer: A. F. A. King suggested that mosquitoes transmit malaria from one person to another.
He proposed this mosquito hypothesis after noting the association between mosquitoes and the occurrence of malaria.

items.followUp: Write two differences between plant and animal cells.

rubric.why: Plant cells have a cell wall, while animal cells do not.
rubric.description: Gives the cell-wall difference.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting the presence and absence of a cell wall.

rubric.why: Plant cells have chloroplasts and typically a large central vacuole; animal cells lack chloroplasts and usually have smaller vacuoles.
rubric.description: Gives another structural difference.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct difference involving chloroplasts or vacuoles.

modelAnswer: A plant cell has a cell wall outside its cell membrane, whereas an animal cell has no cell wall.
Plant cells have chloroplasts and usually a large central vacuole; animal cells lack chloroplasts and generally have smaller vacuoles.
